meta.title: ChatGPT vs. Claude
meta.source: Apple customer-review feeds across seven English-language storefronts
meta.note: The product synthesizes a balanced 480-review panel from 4,992 collected reviews. Results are directional: public reviews overrepresent customers motivated to post, and available history differs by storefront.

executiveInsights.label: Shared friction
executiveInsights.title: The paid boundary is becoming part of the product experience
executiveInsights.summary: Limits, pricing, and upgrade prompts appear more often in the recent window for both products. Customers experience an interrupted task as a product failure, even when the model is performing well.

executiveInsights.label: Competitive difference
executiveInsights.title: Claude is discussed as a workbench; ChatGPT as a broad utility
executiveInsights.summary: Claude’s recent reviews contain more explicit work, coding, and planning language. ChatGPT’s reviews span learning, images, everyday questions, and personal utility more evenly.

executiveInsights.label: Opportunity
executiveInsights.title: Model capability is being judged through mobile task completion
executiveInsights.summary: File handling, copy and paste, uploads, and performance recur beside praise for intelligence. The opportunity is not another model claim; it is helping customers finish the task on the device already in hand.
executiveInsights.metric: Images & files rose 5.0 pp for Claude

problems.title: Limits interrupt high-intent moments
problems.description: Photo, message, and plan limits become most visible after users have already invested in a task.

problems.title: Trust breaks through contradiction
problems.description: Reviewers notice when follow-up questions expose an earlier answer as incomplete or wrong.

problems.title: Utility is broad, but the promise is diffuse
problems.description: Customers move between school, images, business, and everyday advice rather than clustering around one dominant job.

productBriefs.hypothesis: ChatGPT’s reach creates its own expectation: customers assume every task should continue fluidly across messages, media, and plans.
productBriefs.opportunity: Make remaining capacity and fallback paths visible before interruption. Preserve the thread, inputs, and next-best action when a limit is reached.

problems.title: Plan limits overshadow capability
problems.description: Paid customers still describe caps and eligibility as broken promises rather than packaging decisions.

problems.title: Mobile workflows feel incomplete
problems.description: Uploads, file outputs, and iPhone task completion create friction around otherwise high-value work.

problems.title: Behavior changes are highly salient
problems.description: Tone, refusal, and perceived regressions can make an update feel like a different product.

productBriefs.hypothesis: Claude wins consideration for complex work, so customers judge it against an end-to-end professional workflow rather than answer quality alone.
productBriefs.opportunity: Own the mobile completion loop: reliable file handling, clearer plan entitlements, and continuity when a workflow crosses limits or devices.

evidence.quote: You can only send one or a few photos before it asks you to subscribe.
When I asked more questions, it admitted it gave me contradictory information.
Everything from monitoring my solar array to helping me run my business.
Why won’t it let me copy and paste long text?
Even with the paid version they have a limit and want to charge you.
Business needs to be able to run on iPhone, not desktop.
It used to be useful. I just want objective responses.
An organisation tool, a thinking tool, a delivery tool, a nerve centre to your life.
